### 🥁 Not quite my tempo.

This pull request is rushing and dragging at the same time. You attempt to enforce sanitization on localization properties, but your diff calculation blows up with an index out of bounds, your regex doesn't understand ASCII ranges, you pasted Italian into a Lithuanian bundle, and you rammed Java MessageFormat into React i18next property files. Clean this mess up.

**4** finding(s) — 2 critical, 2 warning, 0 suggestion.

**StringIndexOutOfBoundsException in diff slice calculation**

When `start` and `end` overlap on common boundary characters (for instance, if `value` is `" a "` and `sanitized` is `" "`), `start + end` exceeds the length of the string, causing `value.substring(start, value.length() - end)` or `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)` to throw `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` with a negative length. Bound `end` during comparison: `while (end < sanitized.length() - start && end < value.length() - start && ...)`.

_severity: critical · confidence 0.95_

**Broken i18next interpolation syntax in React UI**

The Account UI (and Admin UI) is a React application driven by `i18next`, not Java's `MessageFormat`. Replacing `{{0}}`, `{{1}}`, and `{{2}}` with Java `{0}` choice syntax `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` breaks frontend interpolation completely; the raw choice pattern will be rendered directly on screen to users. _severity: critical · confidence 0.95_

**Regex character class forms unintended ASCII range**

In `[a-zA-Z-_]`, unescaped `-_` between `Z` (ASCII 90) and `_` (ASCII 95) creates an ASCII range matching `Z`, `[`, `\`, `]`, `^`, and `_`. It fails to match an actual hyphen (`-`, ASCII 45). Place the hyphen at the end or escape it: `"_[a-zA-Z_\\-]*\\.properties"`.

_severity: warning · confidence 0.90_

`totpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` is Italian text committed into a Lithuanian (`_lt.properties`) bundle (the same error is present in `theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties`). Provide the proper Lithuanian translation or revert the text change.

review_comments.body:
### 🥁 Not quite my tempo.

This pull request claims to support recovery keys in user storage, but it does not even retrieve them from user storage. The credential lookup completely misses credentials persisted in storage providers, guaranteeing a runtime failure during login, while raw plaintext codes are serialized straight into user credentials. Not acceptable.

**4** finding(s) — 2 critical, 2 warning, 0 suggestion.

**User storage credentials cannot be retrieved via federated or stored credential streams**

Neither getFederatedCredentialsStream() nor getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream() queries credentials managed directly by a UserStorageProvider. When a storage provider handles updateCredential(recoveryCodesCredential), the credential is saved in that provider, not in Keycloak's DB credential tables. Calling getCredential(user) returns Optional.empty() for any user whose codes reside in user storage, which causes RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean to throw NoSuchElementException and causes RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator to re-arm CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES on every login. Query the user's storage provider or route credential retrieval through a mechanism that actually inspects the user storage adapter.

_severity: critical · confidence 0.95_

**Plaintext recovery codes serialized and passed to user storage**

generatedCodes contains the raw, plaintext recovery codes. Serializing plaintext codes into JSON and wrapping them in UserCredentialModel dispatches unhashed credentials to whatever storage provider is configured. Recovery codes are authentication factors and must be stored hashed, exactly as handled by RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.hashRawCode. Pass the hashed representation or credentialModel data instead of raw plaintext strings.

_severity: critical · confidence 0.95_

**Unchecked Optional.get() on credential lookup**

Calling credentialModelOpt.get() directly without validating presence guarantees a NoSuchElementException whenever credential lookup yields Optional.empty(), turning an authentication failure into an unhandled 500 error. Check credentialModelOpt.isPresent() and handle the missing credential explicitly or throw an informative exception.

_severity: warning · confidence 0.90_

**Missing null check on credential provider lookup**

session.getProvider(CredentialProvider.class, "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes") will return null if the provider is unavailable or not registered. When userStorageCreated is false, line 128 invokes createCredential on this reference, triggering a NullPointerException. Verify that recoveryCodeCredentialProvider is non-null before attempting to use it.

golden_comments.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

You introduced provider ordering to resolve classpath collisions, but you failed to handle a unison: when two primary providers tie for top priority, selection falls to non-deterministic classpath loading. **Undetected priority collision between providers**

When multiple providers share the highest order value (for instance, DefaultCryptoProvider, FIPS1402Provider, and WildFlyElytronProvider all specify order 200), sorting by order alone yields an arbitrary winner dictated solely by ServiceLoader iteration order. If foundProviders.size() > 1 and foundProviders.get(0).order() == foundProviders.get(1).order(), throw an IllegalStateException indicating conflicting providers with equal priority instead of silently choosing one.

### 🥁 Not quite my tempo.

You set out to prevent slow batch items from clogging the pipeline, but you rushed the execution and built an engine that drops data, fails on rebalance, and abandons queued work on shutdown. The lifecycle management between Arroyo and your queue pool is completely out of rhythm. Fix the fundamentals before this touches production.

**4** finding(s) — 3 critical, 1 warning, 0 suggestion.

**Unexpected exceptions in submit() mark offsets as completed**

Catching `Exception` in `submit` and immediately invoking `add_offset` followed by `complete_offset` marks failed messages as successfully processed in `OffsetTracker`. If payload decoding, `grouping_fn`, or `work_queue.put` fails, the message is silently dropped and its offset is committed to Kafka without any retry or DLQ routing. Re-raise or route through an explicit DLQ policy instead of treating submission failures as completed offsets.

_severity: critical · confidence 0.95_

**Worker loop terminates before queue drain on shutdown**

`FixedQueuePool.shutdown()` sets `worker.shutdown = True` and calls `q.shutdown(immediate=False)`. However, `OrderedQueueWorker.run()` tests `while not self.shutdown:` on every loop iteration. The moment a worker finishes its active item, it encounters `self.shutdown == True` and breaks, leaving any remaining queued work unprocessed despite `immediate=False`. Rely on `self.work_queue.get()` raising `queue.ShutDown` to break the loop so all pending work items are drained before workers exit.

_severity: critical · confidence 0.95_

**Factory-level queue pool destroyed on consumer rebalance**

`ResultsStrategyFactory` allocates a single `FixedQueuePool` in `__init__`, but `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` calls `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`. When Arroyo revokes partitions on a Kafka rebalance, the active strategy is closed and joins its queue pool, permanently shutting down the queues and workers. When `create_with_partitions` runs post-rebalance, it hands the new strategy the same dead `queue_pool`, breaking message processing permanently. Instantiate the `FixedQueuePool` per strategy in `create_thread_queue_parallel_worker`, or transfer ownership so `close()` does not destroy the factory's shared pool.

_severity: critical · confidence 0.95_

**Asynchronous commit thread bypasses processor lifecycle**

Arroyo's `commit` callback wraps the consumer and is not thread-safe for arbitrary concurrent invocation while the stream processor loop is polling Kafka. Spawning `_commit_loop` in an uncoordinated background thread introduces race conditions. Additionally, `close()` terminates `self.commit_thread` before `queue_pool.shutdown()` finishes draining workers, so offsets completed during shutdown are never committed. Drive offset commits synchronously within `poll()` on the processor thread and flush pending committable offsets in `join()`.

golden_comments.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

review_comments.body:
### 🥁 Not quite my tempo.

You tried to compose a unified OAuth credential sync layer, but you failed to verify whether any of the underlying services were playing the same tune. You wrote invalid Zod schema definitions that evaluate to stringified object literals, returned raw fetch Responses into callers expecting Axios or client SDK outputs, and wrote unparsed SafeParse wrapper structures straight into the database. Take it from the top and ensure your abstraction respects every contract it touches.

**5** finding(s) — 3 critical, 2 warning, 0 suggestion.

**Invalid Zod schema definition via computed property names**

`[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` do not create dynamic schemas in Zod. In JavaScript, both computed property names evaluate at initialization to the string literal `'[object Object]'`, meaning the second declaration overwrites the first. Because Zod strips unconfigured properties by default, this schema strips all actual fields except `access_token` and `[object Object]`. Use `z.record(z.unknown())` or `.passthrough()`, and parse or locate the expiry field explicitly.

_severity: critical · confidence 1.00_

**Persisting Zod SafeParse result object directly into credential key**

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a `SafeParseReturnType` object (`{ success: true, data: ... }`), not the parsed credential object. Storing `key` directly into `prisma.credential.update` saves `{ success: true, data: ... }` to the database. On subsequent loads, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` will fail because the credentials are nested under `data`. Save `key.data` instead: `data: { key: key.data }`.

_severity: critical · confidence 1.00_

**Mismatched return types breaking OAuth callers across integrations**

When credential sharing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response`. Callers in `GoogleCalendarService` expect an object with `.data` (`res?.data`), `zoho-bigin` and `zohocrm` expect Axios responses with `.data`, and `hubspot` expects a `HubspotToken` object. Reading `.data` or token fields directly off of a `Response` throws a `TypeError` at runtime or writes `undefined` to the database. Normalize the return type of `refreshOAuthTokens` across all integrations or adapt the responses within each service before reading token data.

_severity: critical · confidence 1.00_

**Passing credentialId instead of userId to refreshOAuthTokens**

`refreshAccessToken` passes `credentialId` as the third parameter to `refreshOAuthTokens`, which expects `userId: number | null` and forwards it as `calcomUserId`. Pass `credential.userId` to `refreshAccessToken` (or pass the full `credential` object) so that the sync endpoint receives the user's ID rather than the row ID of the credential.

_severity: warning · confidence 0.95_

**Missing HTTP method guard and case-sensitive header lookup**

The webhook handler does not verify the HTTP request method; non-POST requests will proceed to parse `req.body` and fail. Enforce the method: `if (req.method !== 'POST') return res.status(405).json({ message: 'Method not allowed' });`. Furthermore, Node.js lowercases all incoming header keys in `req.headers`, so `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || ...]` will fail if the environment variable contains uppercase characters. Normalize the lookup key with `.toLowerCase()`.

_severity: warning · confidence 0.90_
